Fall Sampling - Many reaches of the streams in the project area were dry from September to November, 1975. Chemical data were collected from four surface-water stations: SW-1 (Sarpy Creek above East Fork Sarpy Creek), SW-2 (East Fork Sarpy Creek above Sarpy Creek), SW-4 (East Fork Sarpy Creek at County Bridge), and SW-5 (Pleasant Creek). The following comments on the data are adapted from Dames and Moore, (1975, p. 17).
The data from fall samples indicated a significant increase in calcium, sodium, and potassium at SW-1 compared to the summertime low-flow results. Decreases of sodium concentrations of about 25 percent occurred at SW-2, SW-4, and SW-5, which are located on tributaries to Sarpy Creek. Sulfate concentrations decreased from 20 to 30 percent compared to summertime low-flow measurements, whereas bicarbonate concentration increases, ranged from about 50 percent at SW-1 to about 10 percent at SW-5. Some increase in strontium occurred at SW-1; however, the concentrations at other stations ranged between previous known values. Concentrations of boron at all stations decreased compared to the low-flow summer results.
